messages:
maria_support: Hey team — getting escalations from a few customers about large p95/p99 spikes since ~09:30 UTC that look correlated with cache miss storms. Support ticket #12345.

Logs show repeated prefix cache misses and rapid evictions for the KV/prefix cache. Example log snippet:

```
[09:31:12] WARN cache.miss prefix=user:session: key=user:session:123
[09:31:12] INFO cache.evict reason=capacity evicted=32 current_size=480MB
[09:31:13] WARN cache.miss prefix=user:session: key=user:session:123 
[09:31:14] WARN cache.miss prefix=user:session: key=user:session:123 
[09:31:14] METRICS cache_hit_rate=0.12 cache_eviction_rate=0.9 p95=860ms p99=2.3s
```

Customer repro steps: high-QPS chat streams hitting same prefix but slightly different keys. Ticket says latency >2s for some calls. Can someone from runtime take a look? :eyes: 

---

kai_runtime: Looking now. Can you paste the trace IDs for a few of the slow requests and the grafana panels (cache_hit_rate, eviction_rate, per-prefix ops)? Also which model and pod pool is affected?

maria_support: Trace IDs attached in the ticket (trace: trace-8f7e, trace-8f8a). Grafana: https://grafana.r/infx/cache_dash?panel=kv_hits (private). Affected model: "open-ggml-chat-1" on hosted-pool-3 (prod-us). Seems concentrated on routes that do prefix-based KV lookups for session state.

jamie_sre: Quick hypothesis: this looks like cache thrash — either eviction threshold too low or keys aren't normalized so slightly different keys miss the prefix cache. Also check if prefix cache is doing exact-match instead of prefix-range. Will check eviction metrics and recent deploys.

omar_platform: I'm seeing a config change 09:15 UTC that reduced per-worker cache quota (we rolled some memory back on prod hosts). Could be collateral. Reverting quota should be low risk. Want me to roll config back to previous cache_quota_mb=600 from 460?

kai_runtime: Before rollback, let's validate whether keys are identical. I ran a quick sample on the canary and found some keys with trailing spaces and inconsistent separators:

```
# sample keys observed
"user:session:123"
"user:session:123 "  # trailing space
"user :session:123"  # accidental space inside prefix
"user:session:123
"
```

If the cache key generation differs across callers we get miss storms even under modest QPS. Recommend adding normalization (trim + collapse whitespace) in keygen, and also add a transient cache warmup after deploy.

maria_support: Nice catch. Ticket notes that calls come from both web-sdk and mobile-sdk versions — maybe a bug in mobile concat.

jamie_sre: Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase cache quota on affected hosts, 2) change eviction to a slightly less aggressive policy (LRU -> CLOCK or LFU-ish), 3) temporarily bypass prefix-matching and fall back to a cheaper local in-memory cache for a minute. We should pick 1+2 for immediate impact.

kai_runtime: I can push a canary patch that normalizes keys and flips eviction policy on canary pool. Patch includes:

```
# key normalization pseudo
def make_cache_key(prefix, id):
    raw = f"{prefix}:{id}"
    normalized = ' '.join(raw.split()).strip()
    return normalized
```

and config change to use CLOCK with slightly larger target_size.

jamie_sre: If we increase cache_quota, be mindful of host OOMs. Omar, do we have headroom on hosted-pool-3?

omar_platform: There's ~20% headroom across pool but some hosts are tight. I can target config on a canary subset of hosts first. I'll hold off full rollback until we validate.

maria_support: I'm going to ping the customers and tell them we're investigating and will roll mitigations in the next 30m.

--- 18m later ---

kai_runtime: Deployed canary: normalized keys + CLOCK eviction on 10% canary hosts + cache_quota bump to 575MB for canary. Observed immediate improvement in canary metrics: cache_miss_rate dropped from 0.88 -> 0.22, p95 reduced 860ms -> 220ms, p99 2.3s -> 360ms.

```
# quick query we ran
sum(rate(cache_miss_total[1m])) by (prefix)
```

maria_support: Confirmed with customer A that latency is improved on their traffic that hit canary hosts. They reported interactive responsiveness back. :tada:

jamie_sre: Good. Next steps: 1) roll normalization + eviction change to all hosts in controlled stages, 2) add unit + fuzz tests for cache key generation to catch whitespace/formatting bugs, 3) add a telemetry guard that alerts if per-prefix miss rate spikes > x% within 5m, 4) plan a background cache-warm job to prepopulate hot prefixes right after deploy.

kai_runtime: Also adding a migration script to collapse duplicate keys in redis backing store (we found duplicate entries due to trailing spaces). Migration plan: identify keys where normalized != raw, copy+delete in batch with rate limit. Will post PR.

omar_platform: I'll coordinate rollout schedule, can do staged rollout over the next 2 hours and keep an eye on cluster memory. Also will revert the earlier config change on non-canary hosts once the normalization is stable.

maria_support: Closing the ticket for now as "mitigation deployed — monitoring". I'll reopen if customers see regressions. Thanks all.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary-deploy successful (canary-id: can-4492). :white_check_mark:

kai_runtime: Post-mortem notes to add: root cause = cache key generation inconsistency + aggressive cache quota change; mitigations = key normalization, moderate cache_quota increase, eviction policy change, warmup and telemetry. Action owners: kai (runtime patch + tests), omar (rollout), jamie (telemetry + alerts), maria (customer comms). ETA for full rollout: 2-3 hours pending smoke tests.

maria_support: Thx everyone. I'll update support ticket and post a short message to #customer-success after full rollout.

jamie_sre: Also adding a short-term automated remediation: if per-prefix miss_rate > 0.5 AND eviction_rate > 0.7 for 2m, auto-increase cache_quota by 20% for that host (bounded) — will prototype after this incident.

kai_runtime: One more note — we should avoid string concatenation for keygen in multiple places. I opened an internal library PR to centralize keygen and enforce normalization. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4521 (internal).

maria_support: Great. Will mark this thread resolved when full rollout completes.
